title: introduce-compact-session-stub-and-retry-factory-triad-sdk-ergonomic-bump
author: Ethan Cole
body:
Motivation: Several teams reported friction when wiring short-lived session tokens and per-request retry policies across SDKs. This PR introduces a compact, language-idiomatic SessionStub + RetryFactory pair that standardizes: (1) a lightweight session lease primitive for optimistic token renewal, (2) a small DSL for common retry profiles (fast-fail, conservative, idempotent-safe), and (3) ergonomic surface changes across Python/TypeScript/Go to reduce ceremony when using streaming pull/push APIs.

What this changes (high-level):
- New SDK-level primitives: SessionStub (py/ts/go) and RetryFactory (py/ts/go). SessionStub exposes an adapter pattern so platform credential providers can plug in without caller boilerplate. RetryFactory provides named presets and a builder for custom backoff composition.
- Python: add contextmanager SessionStub and SessionLease; introduce retry presets in redwood.sdk.retries with small helpers that integrate with existing client.run_stream async iterator helpers. Bumped python SDK to 2.2.0 in the top-level SDK manifest.
- TypeScript: add AbortablePullStream wrapper and compact credential adapter (SessionStubTS). Expose retry presets via a RetryFactory class and typed RetryProfile union. TS SDK bumped to 1.7.0.
- Go: add SessionFactory that returns context-aware session leases, provide RetryFactory with fluent options and a small compatibility shim for existing BackoffConfig. Go SDK module bumped to v1.6.0.
- Tests: unit tests for session renewal races, end-to-end integration of retry presets with streaming reconnects, and cross-language doc examples updated.

Design notes:
- Minimal surface area: the SessionStub is intentionally tiny (Create/Refresh/Revoke) and returns a short-lived token plus TTL. It does not attempt to manage refresh scheduling; instead it offers SessionLease which users can attach to automatic refresh closures shipped by platform credential adapters. This keeps the SDK side-effects explicit.
- RetryFactory presets are conservative by default (sensible retries for idempotent endpoints, fast-fail for non-idempotent streaming writes). The presets are runtime-configurable for advanced users.
- Streaming ergonomics: pull-streams now accept an optional session parameter and a retry profile; both are optional to preserve backward compatibility.

- feat(py): RetryFactory, presets, tests, bump version to 2.2.0
- feat(ts): AbortablePullStream, SessionStubTS adapter, RetryFactory (1.7.0 bump)

review_thread:
Anya Rivera (review): Can we make the Python SessionLease support explicit shutdown to avoid background refresh races?
Ethan Cole (response): Added close() to SessionLease and updated tests to call it in teardown.

Michael Zhang (review): The TS AbortablePullStream looks good but please ensure we don't break existing consumers who pass AbortSignal directly.
Ethan Cole (response): Stream constructor accepts either AbortSignal or Session object now (union typed) and we preserved the old path in overloads.

Priya Nair (review): Consider reducing default retry attempts for non-idempotent streaming writes.
Ethan Cole (response): Updated RetryFactory presets: 'fast-fail' now has 0 retries for write streams and documentation clarifies the semantics.
ci_checks: Unit tests (ts): fail (flaky: test_stream_backoff) -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Introduce compact SessionStub + SessionLease and RetryFactory across SDKs. Python SDK -> 2.2.0, TypeScript SDK -> 1.7.0, Go SDK -> v1.6.0. New ergonomics reduce boilerplate for short-lived credentials and provide named retry presets for streaming and RPC use-cases.
notes_for_backport: No user-facing breaking changes; backport only proposed for the 2.1.x branch if teams want the RetryFactory presets without full version bump. Requires test harness adjustments in python tests to avoid background refresh races.
post_merge_tasks: Publish SDK packages (py wheel, npm, go.mod) and update CDN manifests
Add short 'session+retry' snippet to quickstarts repo
Notify solutions-eng and customer success of new presets
